title: A Closer Look G2 – Chapter 2 Lesson 1: Animal Groups

chapter.d: one big part of a book

lesson.d: a time when a teacher helps you learn something
lesson.ex: We have an English lesson on Monday.

big_idea.ex: The big idea of this lesson is how animals grow and change.

essential.d: very important; you must have it

question.d: something you ask to find out the answer
question.ex: The boy put up his hand to ask a question.

vocabulary.d: the words you know or learn
vocabulary.ex: We learn new vocabulary every week.

explore.d: to look around a new place to learn about it
explore.ex: We explore the park and find bugs.

inquiry.d: asking questions and looking for answers
inquiry.ex: Our class did an inquiry about plants.

activity.d: something you do, often for fun or to learn

read.d: to look at words and understand them
read.ex: I read a book before bed.

together.ex: We play together at break time.

learn.d: to get to know something new
learn.ex: I learn to ride a bike.

look.d: to use your eyes to see something
look.ex: Look at the bird in the tree!

wonder.d: to ask yourself about something you want to know
wonder.ex: I wonder why the sky is blue.

talk.ex: I talk with my friend at lunch.

write.d: to put words on paper with a pencil
write.ex: I write my name on my paper.

quick.d: fast; it does not take a long time
quick.ex: We had a quick snack before school.

lab.d: a room where people do science
lab.ex: We look at a leaf with a microscope in the science lab.

link.ex: There is a link between rain and plants. Rain helps plants grow.

social_studies.d: a school subject about people, places and how we live together
social_studies.ex: In social studies we learn about other countries.

fact.ex: It is a fact that fish live in water.

diagram.d: a picture with lines that shows the parts of something
diagram.ex: The diagram shows the parts of a flower.

model.d: a small copy of a real thing
model.ex: I made a model of a turtle with clay.

collage.d: a picture made by sticking many small pictures on paper
collage.ex: We made a collage of animals from old magazines.

partner.d: a person who works or plays with you
partner.ex: My partner and I did the puzzle together.

picture.ex: I drew a picture of my cat.

group.d: some people or things that are together; to group = to put things together that are the same in some way
group.ex: We put the red blocks in one group and the blue blocks in another group.

classify.d: to put things into groups by how they are the same
classify.ex: We classify the buttons by color.

compare.d: to look at two things to see how they are the same or not the same
compare.ex: Compare the two apples. One is big and one is small.

decide.ex: I decide to wear my red shoes.

put.d: to move something to a place
put.ex: Put your toys in the box.

use.d: to do something with a thing
use.ex: I use a spoon to eat soup.

make.d: to build something or to do something new
make.ex: Mom and I make a cake.

find_out.d: to learn something new by looking or asking
find_out.ex: I want to find out how birds fly.

get.ex: Birds use their beaks to get food.

meet.d: to give or get what is needed
meet.ex: Food and water meet a dog’s needs.

need.d: If you need something, you must have it.

needs.d: the things you must have to live
needs.ex: A cat’s needs are food, water and a home.

help.d: to make something easier for someone
help.ex: I help my mom carry the bags.

keep.d: to make something stay the same way

stay.d: to not change; to be the same

protect.d: to keep safe so nothing hurts it

safe.ex: The baby bird is safe in its nest.

alive.ex: The fish in the bowl is alive and swimming.

live.d: to be alive; or to have your home in a place

lives_n.d: the time when something is alive; lives = more than one life
lives_n.ex: Frogs begin their lives in water as tadpoles.

life_cycle.d: how a living thing is born, grows, has babies, and dies
life_cycle.ex: The life cycle of a chicken: egg, chick, hen.

living_thing.d: something that is alive and grows, like a plant, an animal or a person
living_thing.ex: A tree is a living thing. A rock is not.

change.ex: A caterpillar changes into a butterfly.

die.ex: Plants die if they get no water.

young.ex: The mother cat feeds her young.

feed.ex: I feed my fish every morning.

milk.d: a white drink; mother mammals make it for their babies
milk.ex: The baby goat drinks milk from its mother.

hatch.d: to come out of an egg
hatch.ex: The chick will hatch from the egg.

egg.d: a round thing with a shell; baby birds and other animals come out of it
egg.ex: The hen sat on her eggs.

lay.d: to make an egg come out of your body

baby.d: very young; a very young animal or person
baby.ex: The baby elephant walks with its mom.

female.d: a girl or a woman; in animals, the mother kind
female.ex: The female bird lays the eggs.

larva.d: a baby insect after it comes out of the egg; it looks like a worm
larva.ex: A caterpillar is a larva. It will become a butterfly.

adaptation.d: a body part or a way of acting that helps an animal stay alive
adaptation.ex: A giraffe’s long neck is an adaptation. It helps it eat leaves up high.

act.d: to do things in some way
act.ex: My cat acts scared when it hears thunder.

way.ex: This is the way I tie my shoes.

water.d: what is in rivers, seas and rain; we drink it
water.ex: I drink water after I play.

air.d: what we breathe; we cannot see it
air.ex: I blow air into the red balloon.

shelter.d: a safe place to live, away from rain and cold
shelter.ex: A rabbit’s hole is its shelter.

land.ex: Frogs can live on land and in water.

place.ex: A park is a fun place to play.

different.ex: The two cats are different colors.

alike.d: the same or almost the same

kind.d: a group of things that are the same in some way
kind.ex: There are many kinds of apples.

thousand.ex: Thousands of stars are in the sky.

main.ex: This is the main door of our school.

more.ex: I have more stickers than my brother.

most.ex: Most of the apples are red. One is green.

only.ex: He is the only boy with a red hat.

hard.d: not soft; strong like a rock
hard.ex: A turtle has a hard shell.

rough.d: not smooth; bumpy when you touch it

smooth.d: flat and nice to touch, with no bumps

scaly.d: covered with small hard flat pieces called scales

outer.ex: A nut has a hard outer shell.

blue.ex: I fly my blue kite in the sky.

without.ex: A worm is an animal without legs.

breathe.d: to take air into your body and let it out
breathe.ex: Take a deep breath. Breathe in and out.

swim.d: to move in water with your arms, legs or fins
swim.ex: I swim in the pool in summer.

climb.d: to go up something using your hands and feet
climb.ex: The cat can climb the tree.

feel.d: to touch something to know what it is like

taste.d: to know if food is sweet, sour or salty with your tongue
taste.ex: Taste the lemon. It is sour!

smell.d: to know something with your nose

sting.d: to hurt with a sharp point

scientist.d: a person who asks questions and does tests to learn about the world
scientist.ex: The scientist looks at a leaf.

animal.d: a living thing that can move and eat, like a dog, a fish or a bird
animal.ex: My favorite animal is the panda.

mammal.d: an animal with hair or fur; the mother makes milk for her babies

amphibian.d: an animal like a frog; it starts life in water and has moist skin

reptile.d: an animal with dry, scaly skin, like a snake or a turtle

insect.d: a small animal with six legs and a body in three parts, like an ant or a bee

bird.d: an animal with feathers, wings and a beak
bird.ex: The bird sings in the tree.

bluebird.d: a small bird with blue feathers and an orange chest
bluebird.ex: A bluebird sat on our fence.

fish.d: an animal that lives in water and swims with fins
fish.ex: The fish swims in the river.

salmon.d: a big fish that is pink inside; it lives in rivers and the sea
salmon.ex: The bear caught a salmon in the river.

salamander.d: a small amphibian with a long tail and four legs
salamander.ex: A salamander hides under wet leaves.

alligator.d: a big reptile with strong jaws and a long tail; it lives in rivers
alligator.ex: The alligator swims in the river.

lion.d: a big wild cat; the father has long hair around his head
lion.ex: The lion is the king of the animals.

crab.d: a sea animal with a hard shell and ten legs; two of its legs are big claws
crab.ex: The crab walks sideways on the beach.

iguana.d: a big lizard (a kind of reptile) with spikes on its back
iguana.ex: The iguana sits in the sun on a rock.

butterfly.d: an insect with big colorful wings
butterfly.ex: A butterfly sits on a leaf.

snake.d: a long reptile with no legs
snake.ex: The snake moves on the ground.

jellyfish.d: a soft sea animal with long arms that can sting
jellyfish.ex: Don’t touch a jellyfish at the beach!

beetle.d: an insect with a hard shiny back
beetle.ex: A green beetle is on the leaf.

dragonfly.d: an insect with a long thin body and four clear wings
dragonfly.ex: A dragonfly flies over the pond.

crayfish.d: a small water animal like a little lobster, with a hard shell and two claws
crayfish.ex: The crayfish hides under a rock in the stream.

earthworm.d: a long, thin, soft animal that lives in the soil; it has no legs
earthworm.ex: The earthworm comes out after the rain.

body.d: all of a person or an animal
body.ex: Running is good for your body.

part.d: one piece of a whole thing
part.ex: A wheel is a part of a bike.

backbone.d: the long line of bones down the middle of the back
backbone.ex: You have a backbone. Touch your back!

hair.d: thin threads that grow on your head and on some animals

fur.d: the soft thick hair on an animal
fur.ex: My rabbit has soft white fur.

feathers.d: the soft light things that cover a bird

wings.d: the parts a bird or an insect uses to fly

beak.d: the hard mouth of a bird
beak.ex: The bird holds a worm in its beak.

gills.d: the parts on the side of a fish that help it breathe in water
gills.ex: A fish breathes with its gills.

fins.d: the flat parts on a fish that help it swim
fins.ex: The fish moves its fins to swim.

lungs.d: the two parts inside your chest that fill with air when you breathe

skin.d: the outside cover of a body
skin.ex: Wear a hat to protect your skin from the sun.

legs.d: the parts of the body you walk with

antenna.d: one of the two long thin parts on an insect’s head; it helps the insect feel, taste and smell; antennae = more than one antenna

shell.d: a hard cover on the outside of some animals
shell.ex: The snail goes into its shell.

covering.ex: A turtle has a hard covering called a shell.

enemy.d: an animal or person that wants to hurt you
enemy.ex: The cat is the mouse’s enemy.

stage.d: one step in how something grows or changes
stage.ex: A tadpole is one stage in the life of a frog.

galapagos.d: a group of islands in the ocean, west of South America; many special animals live there
galapagos.ex: Giant turtles live on the Galapagos Islands.
